source_text: Hoc semper fuit maximum inter Manichaeos Catholicosque discrimen, et limes quidam latissimus, quo a se mutuo piorum et impiorum dogmata separantur, immo magna moles sententias nostras quasi coeli a terra profunditate disiungens, quod nos omne peccatum voluntati malae, illi vero malae conscribunt naturae; qui cum diversos sequuntur errores, sed velut de capite fontis istius effluentes consequenter ad sacrilegia flagitiaque perveniunt; sicut Catholici e regione, a bono inchoantes exordio, bonis aucti processibus, ad religionis summam, quam ratio munit et pietas, pervehuntur. Tu igitur malum naturale conatus asserere profano quidem voto, sed inefficaci intentione usurpasti Apostoli testimonium, quem hac eadem perscriptione ostendo nihil tale sensisse, quale tu persuadere conaris, quod repugnantibus modis et illum catholicum confiteris, et dicta eius Manichaeo aestimas suffragari.
pass_a_gloss: This has always been the greatest distinction between Manichaeans and Catholics, and a certain very wide boundary by which the dogmas of the pious and of the impious are separated from one another, nay a great mass disjoining our sentences as if by the depth of heaven from earth, that we ascribe every sin to an evil will, but they to an evil nature; who, although they follow diverse errors, yet flowing as if from the head of that fountain, consequently arrive at sacrileges and shameful deeds; just as Catholics from the other side, beginning from a good starting-point, increased by good advances, are carried through to the height of religion, which reason fortifies and piety. You therefore, having tried to assert a natural evil, with a profane wish indeed but an ineffective aim, usurped the testimony of the Apostle, whom by this same writing I show to have sensed nothing such as you try to persuade, because in clashing ways you both confess him catholic and estimate his sayings to vote for a Manichaean.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: This has always been the greatest distinction between Manichaeans and catholics, the broadest boundary separating the doctrines of the devout from those of the impious, indeed a vast barrier dividing our opinions as widely as heaven is separated from earth: we assign every sin to an evil will; they assign it to an evil nature. They pursue various errors, all flowing, as it were, from this fountainhead, and consistently arrive at sacrilege and shameful deeds. Catholics, by contrast, start from a good beginning, advance through good steps, and reach the height of religion, fortified by reason and piety. You therefore tried to establish an evil inherent in nature and appropriated the apostle's testimony for an impious purpose, though to no effect. In this very work I show that the apostle held nothing like the view you are trying to persuade us to accept. You contradict yourself: you acknowledge that he was catholic, yet suppose his words support a Manichaean.

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
